question: A person saves 60% of his income. If his expenditure is ₹480, then his income (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Savings = 60% → Expenditure = 100% − 60% = 40%

Unitary Method: 40% → 480

1% → 480 ÷ 40 = 12

Income (100%) → 12 × 100 = 1200

**∴ Answer = 1200**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Savings percentage = 60%

Expenditure amount = ₹480

**Formula used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Expenditure % = 100% − Savings %

 Total Income (100%) 
• Expenditure (40%) = ₹480 
• Savings (60%) Income = 480 ÷ 0.4 = ₹1200 

**Calculations:**

Let the total income be ₹I.

⇒ Expenditure % = 100% − 60% = 40%

⇒ 40% of I = 480

⇒ (40 ÷ 100) × I = 480

⇒ I = (480 × 100) ÷ 40

⇒ I = 12 × 100 = 1200

**∴ The correct answer is 1200 (Option 2).**
